reasoning: Recent high-quality public polls of the Iowa 2026 U.S. Senate race show a very close contest, with one Emerson College/Nexstar poll giving Republican Ashley Hinson a roughly 3‑point lead over Democrat Josh Turek, while a Fox News poll from late June (still being cited in late July coverage) showed Turek ahead by 4 points; media syntheses like VoteHub’s average and Newsweek/Idaho Public Press write‑ups describe the race as having shifted to a narrow Democratic edge, but individual polls remain within the margin of error.[1][2][3][5][6][7][11] Major forecasters such as Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball continue to rate the Iowa Senate race as "leans Republican," indicating that, structurally and in expert judgment, Republicans retain a small advantage even as recent polling suggests a near toss‑up.[1][2][12] There is no credible, state‑specific general‑election presidential polling for Iowa in the last 45 days, so the best current read is that the Senate race is approximately R+1 to D+1 based on polls, but overall expert consensus still leans slightly R in this environment.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling / Nexstar Media
sources.details: Emerson College/Nexstar likely-voter poll of Iowa found Ashley Hinson at 48% and Josh Turek at 45% in the U.S. Senate race, a 3-point Republican lead within the margin of error.

sources.name: Bleeding Heartland (summarizing Emerson College/Nexstar poll)
sources.details: Bleeding Heartland’s analysis of the Emerson poll reports Hinson ahead of Turek 47.5% to 45.0%, again about a 2.5-point Republican edge, and describes the race as close and within the margin of error.

sources.name: Fox News poll (reported by Newsweek)
sources.details: A Fox News poll of Iowa registered voters found Josh Turek leading Ashley Hinson 50% to 46% in the Senate race, a 4-point Democratic edge, with coverage noting it as part of a warning sign for Republicans in key Senate contests.

sources.name: Des Moines Register (citing NYT/Siena and Fox News polls)
sources.details: Des Moines Register’s profile of the race cites a Fox News poll showing Turek ahead 50% to 46% and a New York Times/Siena poll showing Hinson ahead 48% to 46%, and notes Fox rating the race a "toss-up" while Cook and Sabato still call it "lean Republican."

sources.name: New York Times/Siena poll (via Des Moines Register summary)
sources.details: The New York Times/Siena poll of Iowa adults/likely voters found Hinson leading Turek by 2 points, 48% to 46%, indicating a slight Republican edge but still a close race.

sources.name: Iowa Capital Dispatch (summarizing Fox News & NYT/Siena, Cook rating change)
sources.details: Iowa Capital Dispatch notes that early-July polls showed a tight Senate race, with Turek leading a Fox News poll by 4 points and Hinson leading a NYT/Siena poll by 2 points, and reports Cook Political Report shifting its rating from "likely Republican" to "leans Republican."

sources.name: Global Strategy Group internal poll (via NewsBreak/Politico reporting)
sources.details: NewsBreak/aggregated coverage referencing Politico notes an internal Global Strategy Group poll for Turek’s campaign showing him leading 47% to 45% among 1,000 likely voters, a 2-point Democratic edge.
sources.date_range: Internal poll date not specified (reported July 30, 2026)

sources.name: VoteHub polling average (via Idaho Public Press)
sources.details: Idaho Public Press summary of VoteHub’s July 21 polling averages reports that Iowa’s Senate race moved from a 0.7-point Republican lead in April to a 0.5-point Democratic lead in July, indicating Democrats have edged slightly ahead in the polling average.
sources.date_range: July 21, 2026 (roundup reference, underlying polls in June-July 2026)

sources.name: Inside Elections 2026 Senate Ratings (via 270toWin)
sources.details: 270toWin’s page summarizing Inside Elections 2026 Senate ratings lists Iowa as "Lean Republican," indicating that expert forecasters still consider the GOP slightly favored despite close polling.

sources.name: Cook Political Report & Sabato’s Crystal Ball ratings (via Iowa Capital Dispatch and Des Moines Register)
sources.details: Iowa Capital Dispatch and Des Moines Register report that Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball rate the Iowa Senate race as "leans Republican" even after Cook moved it from "likely" to "leans," suggesting a small but real GOP advantage.

sources.name: NBC News Iowa Senate Primary Election 2026 Live Results
sources.details: NBC News live results page for the Iowa Senate primaries shows Ashley Hinson and Josh Turek winning their respective primaries decisively, but does not provide any general-election margin or lean.
